metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code (server.js) with a deployable entry point (Express server on port 8080), a dependency manifest (package.json), a Dockerfile, CloudFormation IaC, and Kubernetes manifests present — single-service application repository.
metadata.archetype_justification: No database write operations detected; GET /rates queries MongoDB (read-only), POST /quote performs stateless computation. Read-heavy data access with minimal business logic. Classified as data-gateway.

findings.title: Managed Compute
findings.description: The application runs on a single EC2 instance under the forever process manager. CloudFormation references a single AppInstanceId as the ALB target. Dockerfile and K8s manifests exist but are not yet deployed.
findings.gap: All compute is on raw EC2 with no managed container orchestration or serverless. No ECS, EKS, Fargate, or Lambda in use.
findings.recommendation: Deploy the existing containerization artifacts (Dockerfile + K8s manifests) to Amazon EKS or ECS Fargate. The Dockerfile is production-ready (multi-stage, non-root, healthcheck).

findings.title: Managed Databases
findings.description: MongoDB is self-managed on a private instance at 10.0.8.20:27017 with no authentication. No managed database resources found in IaC.
findings.gap: All databases are self-managed with no automated failover, backup, or patching. MongoDB 2.4 is 10 years past EOL.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon DocumentDB (MongoDB-compatible) or DynamoDB for automated backups, Multi-AZ failover, and managed patching.

findings.title: Network Security
findings.description: CloudFormation defines a security group with 0.0.0.0/0 ingress on port 80. No HTTPS listener (blocked since 2019). API key transmitted in cleartext over public internet.
findings.gap: Overly permissive security group. No HTTPS/TLS. No private subnet isolation for the application tier.
findings.recommendation: Add HTTPS listener with ACM certificate. Restrict security group ingress to known partner CIDRs. Move compute to private subnets.

findings.title: API Entry Point
findings.description: Internet-facing ALB with target group and health check. No authentication, throttling, request validation, or HTTPS.
findings.gap: ALB has minimal configuration — no auth, no rate limiting, no WAF, no TLS.
findings.recommendation: Add AWS WAF for rate limiting. Add API Gateway for throttling and auth offload. Enable HTTPS with ACM.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling
findings.description: No auto-scaling configuration. ALB targets a single EC2 instance. All capacity is statically provisioned.
findings.gap: No auto-scaling — workload cannot respond to traffic spikes or scale down during low demand.
findings.recommendation: Configure HPA on EKS when deployed. Enable DocumentDB read replica auto-scaling.

findings.title: Backup and Recovery
findings.description: No backup configuration for MongoDB. S3 bucket has no versioning. No aws_backup_plan or PITR configuration.
findings.gap: No automated backups. Data loss from an incident would be unrecoverable.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to DocumentDB for automated backups with PITR. Enable S3 versioning on rate-card bucket.

findings.title: High Availability and Fault Isolation
findings.description: Single EC2 instance, single MongoDB instance. No multi-AZ fault isolation at compute or data tier.
findings.gap: Single points of failure at both application and database tiers. An AZ failure takes down the entire service.
findings.recommendation: Deploy to EKS across multiple AZs. Migrate to DocumentDB with Multi-AZ.

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage
findings.description: CloudFormation covers ALB, security group, target group, listener, and S3 bucket. EC2, MongoDB, monitoring, DNS, and secrets are not in IaC. Estimated ~30-40% coverage.
findings.gap: Significant manual infrastructure. Only the edge layer is codified.
findings.recommendation: Expand IaC to cover compute (EKS), database (DocumentDB), monitoring (CloudWatch), DNS (Route 53), and secrets (Secrets Manager).

findings.title: CI/CD Automation
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. Deployment is manual: SSH, git pull, forever restart. No automated build, test, or deploy stages.
findings.gap: All deployments are manual. No automated quality gates, no reproducible builds.
findings.recommendation: Implement CI/CD pipeline (CodePipeline + CodeBuild) with lint, test, Docker build, ECR push, and EKS deploy stages.

findings.title: Programming Languages
findings.description: Node.js 0.10.x (EOL 2016) with Express 3.4.8 (EOL) and MongoDB driver 1.4.7. All three axes are end-of-life.
findings.gap: Compound legacy: runtime EOL, framework EOL, database driver severely outdated.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade to Node.js 20 LTS, Express 4.x or Fastify, and MongoDB driver 6.x.

findings.title: API Versioning Strategy
findings.description: No API versioning. Endpoints are /rates and /quote with no version prefix or headers.
findings.gap: No versioning strategy — breaking changes break all consumers simultaneously.
findings.recommendation: Add URL-based versioning (/v1/rates, /v1/quote). Document the API contract in OpenAPI format.

findings.title: Service Discovery
findings.description: MongoDB endpoint is hardcoded in server.js (10.0.8.20:27017). Application code does not read environment variables for service endpoints.
findings.gap: All service endpoints hardcoded. No dynamic discovery, no env-based configuration.
findings.recommendation: Refactor to read MONGO_URL from process.env. On EKS, use Kubernetes DNS for service discovery.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage
findings.description: S3 bucket for carrier rate cards with public access blocked. No automated parsing or extraction pipeline for rate card documents.
findings.gap: Data in S3 but no automated parsing, indexing, or extraction pipeline.
findings.recommendation: Add Lambda trigger on S3 PutObject to parse rate cards and update rates database. Consider Textract for PDF parsing.

findings.title: Unified Data Access Layer
findings.description: Database access embedded directly in Express route handler. MongoClient.connect() called inline with query built from request parameters. No repository pattern or data access abstraction.
findings.gap: No data access layer. Database logic interleaved with HTTP handling.
findings.recommendation: Extract a rates repository module encapsulating MongoDB access for testability and future migration.

findings.title: Database Engine Version and EOL
findings.description: MongoDB 2.4 (implied by driver 1.4.7 compatibility). MongoDB 2.4 reached EOL in 2016 — 10 years past EOL. No version pinning in IaC.
findings.gap: Database engine 10 years past EOL. No version pinning. Known security vulnerabilities unpatched.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon DocumentDB (MongoDB 5.0 compatible) to eliminate version lifecycle management.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest
findings.description: S3 bucket has no BucketEncryption property. MongoDB is self-managed with no encryption at rest. No KMS key resources in the repository.
findings.gap: No encryption at rest on any data store.
findings.recommendation: Add BucketEncryption with SSE-KMS to CloudFormation. DocumentDB enables encryption at rest by default upon migration.

findings.title: API Authentication
findings.description: Static API key (ship-2013-abc123-static) checked via x-api-key header. Hardcoded in source. Transmitted in cleartext over HTTP.
findings.gap: Static API key auth without token-based auth. Shared across all consumers with no per-client identity.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to JWT/OAuth2 via Amazon Cognito or API Gateway authorizer. Enable HTTPS immediately.

findings.title: Centralized Identity Integration
findings.description: Application manages its own authentication entirely with a hardcoded static API key. No IdP integration.
findings.gap: No centralized identity integration. Auth is isolated from organizational identity systems.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with Amazon Cognito for centralized identity with JWT tokens and organizational SSO.

findings.title: Secrets Management
findings.description: Plaintext credentials in server.js: API key and MongoDB connection string hardcoded and committed to git.
findings.gap: Critical: plaintext secrets in source code. Credentials exposed in version control history.
findings.recommendation: Rotate credentials immediately. Move all secrets to AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation. Use EKS secrets store CSI driver.

findings.title: Compute Hardening and Patching
findings.description: No patching strategy for EC2. No SSM, no Inspector, no vulnerability scanning. No Dependabot/Renovate. Known CVEs in dependencies unpatched.
findings.gap: No patching, no vulnerability scanning, no dependency update automation.
findings.recommendation: Add Dependabot for dependency updates. Enable Inspector for container scanning. Use EKS managed node groups for OS patching.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline
findings.description: No security scanning tools. No SAST, no dependency scanning, no container scanning. No CI/CD pipeline exists at all.
findings.gap: No security validation — vulnerabilities reach production undetected.
findings.recommendation: Add npm audit, Snyk/Dependabot for dependency scanning, ECR image scanning, and CodeGuru for SAST when CI/CD is implemented.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing
findings.description: No distributed tracing. No OpenTelemetry, no X-Ray SDK, no tracing libraries in dependencies.
findings.gap: No tracing capability for debugging production issues.
findings.recommendation: Add AWS X-Ray SDK or OpenTelemetry. Use ADOT collector as sidecar on EKS.

findings.title: SLO Definitions
findings.description: No SLO definitions. No CloudWatch alarms. No monitoring configuration in the repository.
findings.gap: No formal service level definitions. No monitoring to detect degradation.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs (p99 latency < 200ms, availability > 99.9%). Add CloudWatch alarms on ALB metrics.

findings.title: Business Metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics published. No business metric instrumentation.
findings.gap: No visibility into business outcomes.
findings.recommendation: Add CloudWatch metrics for quotes_calculated, quote_value, rate_lookups_by_route.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection and Alerting
findings.description: No alerting configured. No CloudWatch alarms or anomaly detection.
findings.gap: No alerting on error rates or latency. Issues discovered by users.
findings.recommendation: Add CloudWatch alarms on ALB 5XX rate, target response time, unhealthy host count.

findings.title: Deployment Strategy
findings.description: Manual deployment: SSH, git pull, forever restart. No staged rollout, no canary, no blue/green.
findings.gap: Direct-to-production with no staged rollout or automated rollback.
findings.recommendation: Deploy to EKS with rolling updates. Upgrade to canary using Argo Rollouts.

findings.title: Integration Testing
findings.description: No automated tests of any kind. No test framework, no test files, no test scripts.
findings.gap: Zero automated quality gates. Code changes cannot be validated automatically.
findings.recommendation: Add Jest + Supertest. Create integration tests for /rates and /quote. Add npm test to CI pipeline.

findings.title: Incident Response Automation
findings.description: No runbooks, no automation, no self-healing. Only response is manual SSH access.
findings.gap: No documented or automated incident response.
findings.recommendation: Create runbooks for common incidents. On EKS, leverage pod restart on probe failure. Add SSM Automation for escalation.

findings.title: Observability Ownership
findings.description: No observability ownership. No CODEOWNERS, no dashboards, no alarm ownership.
findings.gap: No team accountable for service health metrics.
findings.recommendation: Add CODEOWNERS file. Create CloudWatch dashboard. Assign alarm ownership to service team.

findings.title: Resource Tagging Governance
findings.description: No tags on any CloudFormation resources. ALB, security group, target group, and S3 bucket all lack tags.
findings.gap: No resource tagging. Cannot attribute costs or identify ownership.
findings.recommendation: Add tags to all resources: Service, Environment, Owner, CostCenter.

evaluations.title: Workflow Orchestration
evaluations.reason: Score 4 — no multi-step workflows exist; data-gateway archetype correctly has no workflow orchestration needs.

evaluations.title: Async Messaging and Streaming
evaluations.reason: Score 4 — synchronous HTTP is the correct design for this data-gateway archetype. No async messaging needed.

evaluations.title: Monolith vs Microservices
evaluations.reason: Score 4 — single-purpose service with clear boundaries, independently deployable, no circular dependencies.

evaluations.title: Async vs Sync Communication
evaluations.reason: Score 4 — synchronous reads are correct for data-gateway archetype. No cross-service async needed.

evaluations.title: Long-Running Process Handling
evaluations.reason: Score 4 — no operations exceed 30 seconds. Simple DB query and arithmetic computation.

evaluations.title: Stored Procedures and Schema Complexity
evaluations.reason: Score 4 — no stored procedures or proprietary SQL. All business logic in application layer.

evaluations.title: Audit Logging
evaluations.reason: Audit logging (CloudTrail) is an account-level concern. This repo contains only application-level IaC (ALB, S3 bucket). CloudTrail evaluation belongs in the foundation infrastructure repo.
